h1: The 7 Best AirPrint Printers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven wireless printers for iPhone and iPad users, compared on confirmed AirPrint, ink cost, scanning and home office features.
summary: The Canon TS5320 is the best overall pick because its listing names AirPrint outright. The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the best pick for frequent printing without cartridge costs, the HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e suits home offices that need an automatic document feeder, and the Canon PIXMA TR4720 leads for scanning.
intro: The word AirPrint is on many printer boxes but missing from many product listings, which is the catch for shoppers. A printer can work with iPhone printing and still fail to say so on its page, leaving you to verify it yourself. If you want certainty before you buy, the listing itself is the first filter.

We reviewed seven wireless printers and ranked them on whether AirPrint is named in writing, plus ink system, scanning, duplex and document feeder features. Only one of the seven names AirPrint on its listing. For the others, you can confirm compatibility in Apple's support list or the manufacturer's page before ordering.

products.name: Canon TS5320 All-in-One Wireless Printer with AirPrint
products.verdict: The only printer here that names AirPrint right on the listing.
products.description:
A compact wireless all-in-one that prints, scans and copies, with AirPrint named explicitly in the product title. It sits in the $100-200 bucket and supports Amazon Dash Replenishment.

It ranks first because it removes the guesswork that the other six picks leave open. Against the Epson EcoTank below, it uses cartridges, so running costs may be higher over time.

Choose it if you want certainty that iPhone printing works. Light home use suits it best.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want AirPrint confirmed in writing.
products.skipIf: You print heavily and want low ink cost.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A cartridge-free tank printer for people who print often.
products.description:
A wireless cartridge-free supertank printer with scan and copy functions and the Epson Smart Panel app. It sits in the $100-200 bucket. The listing does not name AirPrint, so check it before buying.

It ranks second since the ink tanks lower the cost of each page, a major advantage over the Canon TS5320 for frequent printers. The AirPrint claim is not in the listing, which is the only reason it sits below.

Best for iPhone users who print regularly and want to avoid cartridge refills. Be prepared to fill the tanks yourself.
products.idealFor: Frequent printers who dislike buying cartridges.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: ADF and duplex printing for a home workspace.
products.description:
A color inkjet that scans and copies, with a sheet feeder that handles stacks of pages, two-sided printing, a 3-month Instant Ink trial and the HP Smart app as a fallback for mobile printing. It sits in the $50-100 bucket. AirPrint is not named on the listing.

It ranks third because the feeder and duplex printing give it the most office capability, but the AirPrint claim must be checked. Against the Canon TR4720 below, it is the more office-oriented choice.

A fit for a home office that prints and scans multi-page documents. Verify AirPrint compatibility first.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: An auto document feeder and mobile support at a low price.
products.description:
A color inkjet all-in-one with an auto document feeder, mobile printing support and a built-in fax. It lies in the $50-100 bucket. AirPrint is not named on the listing.

It ranks fourth because it lacks the duplex printing of the HP above, but it keeps the feeder at a similar price. Its fax is a legacy feature that most households will skip.

Best for people who scan documents to a phone as often as they print. Confirm AirPrint before ordering.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small OLED screen shows Wi-Fi status messages.
products.description:
A color inkjet with duplex printing and a 1.42 inch OLED display that shows network status messages. It lies in the $50-100 bucket. AirPrint is not named on the listing.

It ranks fifth because the display helps you fix Wi-Fi problems, though it has no feeder like the picks above. It suits a compact desk.

Choose it if you expect to wrestle with network setup. Verify AirPrint before buying.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want help with Wi-Fi setup.
products.skipIf: You need to scan stacks of pages.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A low-cost print, scan and copy machine with an ink trial.
products.description:
A compact color inkjet all-in-one with a 3-month Instant Ink trial and a simple wireless setup flow, in the $50-100 bucket. AirPrint is not named on the listing.

It ranks sixth because it offers no duplex or feeder, features present on pricier models above. The strength is a very approachable setup and a low entry price.

A fit for light home use and students. Confirm AirPrint yourself before buying.
products.skipIf: You print a lot of documents.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Duplex printing and a copier/scanner in a compact tray design.
products.description:
A color inkjet with duplex printing, a built-in copier and scanner, a compact single-tray design and mobile app printing support. It sits in the $50-100 bucket. AirPrint is not named.

It ranks last because it has no display and no feeder, so it has fewer helpers than the TS6520 or TR4720. Canon's app is a fallback if AirPrint does not connect.

Good for budget buyers who will verify AirPrint themselves. Look at it for tight desk space.
products.skipIf: You want a feeder or screen.

whatMatters.detail: AirPrint lets an iPhone or iPad print wirelessly without installing a driver. It matters because it avoids app setup. Look for the word AirPrint in the title, or check Apple's compatibility list before buying.

Cartridge printers have a low upfront price but a higher cost per page, while tank printers cost more initially and far less to run. If you print weekly, tanks save money. Look for the terms ink tank or cartridge-free.
An automatic feeder scans or copies multiple pages without lifting the lid each time. It saves time on contracts and forms. Check the listing for ADF.
Automatic two-sided printing halves paper use and suits reports. Without it, you flip pages by hand. Look for duplex in the specs.
Wireless setup is where many users get stuck. A display or a guided app flow helps. Check whether the listing mentions a control panel or app setup.

faq.q: How do I know if a printer supports AirPrint?
faq.a: Look for AirPrint in the product title or specs, or check the manufacturer's compatibility list. Only the Canon TS5320 names it in its listing here.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Assuming every Wi-Fi printer supports AirPrint. Some use proprietary apps only, so verify before buying.

faq.q: Is an EcoTank worth it over a cartridge printer?
faq.a: If you print often, yes, since ink costs drop sharply. For light use, a cartridge model costs less upfront.

faq.q: How do I set up AirPrint?
faq.a: Connect the printer and iPhone to the same Wi-Fi network, then tap the share icon and choose Print.

faq.q: How do I maintain an inkjet?
faq.a: Print something every couple of weeks so the ink does not dry in the nozzles, and run the head cleaning only when quality drops.

faq.q: What if the printer does not show up on my iPhone?
faq.a: Check that both are on the same network, restart both, and confirm the printer's wireless setup is complete.

finalTake: The Canon TS5320 is the safe pick for iPhone owners because AirPrint is confirmed in the title. The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is better for heavy use, and the HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e suits home offices. For any printer whose listing does not name AirPrint, verify compatibility before you buy.
